beats.say: Solve four to the power X, minus three times two to the power X, plus two, equals zero.
Four steps: first the same base, then substitute, then solve the quadratic, and last bring back X.
Step one, same base. The other term is two to the power X, so write four with base two too.
Four is two squared, so four to the power X is two squared, to the power X.
Times power: multiply the powers, two times X. That gives two to the power two X.
So the equation becomes two to the power two X, minus three times two to the power X, plus two, equals zero.
Look at the powers: two X is the same as X times two.
asks: Why is 2x the same as x times 2?

beats.say: So by times power, two to the power two X is two to the power X, all squared.
asks: Why is 2 to the 2x the same as (2 to the x) squared?

beats.say: Now the equation has two to the power X, and two to the power X, all squared. A quadratic in disguise.

do.on: two to the power X, and

beats.say: Step two, substitute: let A equal two to the power X.
asks: Can I use u instead of a?

beats.say: Then two to the power X, all squared, is A squared.
asks: Where does a squared come from?

beats.say: And three times two to the power X is three times A.
asks: Why is 3 times 2 to the x equal to 3a?

beats.say: So the equation becomes A squared minus three A plus two equals zero.
asks: Is this a normal quadratic now?

beats.say: Step three, solve the quadratic. It factorises into A minus two, times A minus one.
So A equals two, or A equals one. Both are positive, as two to the power X always is.
Step four, bring back X. The question asks for X, so each value of A gives a value of X.
asks: Why can't I stop at a?

beats.say: A equals two: two to the power X is two, which is two to the power one.
asks: Why write 2 as 2 to the power 1?

do.on: two to the power X is two

beats.say: Both sides have base two, so the powers are equal: X equals one.
asks: Why can I compare the powers?

beats.say: A equals one: two to the power X is one, which is two to the power zero. So X equals zero.
asks: Why is 1 the same as 2 to the power 0?

do.on: two to the power X is one

beats.say: So X equals one, or X equals zero.
